concepts.title: Sets and Their Representations: Roster and Set Builder Forms
concepts.definition: A set is a well defined collection of objects, represented in roster form by listing elements or in set builder form by a property, with symbols of belongs to and does not belong to, and empty, finite and infinite sets classified by their elements.
concepts.key_idea: The chapter builds the vocabulary of sets, from empty and finite infinite sets to equal sets, that later chapters on relations and functions use.

concepts.title: Union, Intersection and Complement of Sets
concepts.definition: Sets combine by union of elements in either set, intersection of common elements, difference of elements in one set not the other, and complement of elements outside a set within the universal set, and these obey laws of commutativity, associativity and distributivity.
concepts.key_idea: The cardinal number formula ties counting of elements to the set operations, and De Morgan's laws connect union, intersection and complement.

concepts.title: Subsets, Power Set, Intervals and Venn Diagrams
concepts.definition: A set A is a subset of B when every element of A lies in B, the power set holds all subsets with cardinality 2 to the power n, and intervals of the real line are written with open and closed brackets, with Venn diagrams picturing set relations.
concepts.key_idea: Intervals like open, closed and half open are themselves sets of real numbers, and Venn diagrams show subset, union and intersection visually.
